summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with worsening dyspnea, chronic right-sided low back pain, subjective fevers, and urinary frequency. She had significant hypoxia on admission with oxygen saturation of 83% on room air and bilateral lower extremity edema. Evaluation revealed pulmonary edema in the setting of decompensated diastolic heart failure. She was treated with intravenous furosemide twice daily, resulting in a 7.5 kg weight loss and improved oxygenation to 86–91% on room air. A V/Q scan ruled out pulmonary embolism. Chronic back pain was noted to have degenerative changes on imaging, but no acute intervention was performed. Urinary frequency and pyuria were attributed to asymptomatic bacteriuria, and antibiotics were discontinued. She remained afebrile inpatient. A nodular liver contour on CT raised concern for early cirrhosis, prompting recommendation for hepatology follow-up. She was discharged home with services on oral furosemide and potassium, with instructions to monitor daily weight and follow up for management of heart failure, liver disease, and chronic pain.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic (congestive) heart failure
Unspecified viral hepatitis B without hepatic coma
Unspecified viral hepatitis C without hepatic coma
Personal history of malignant neoplasm of ovary
